meta.move: Strong path to the last position
meta.expect: Moves one position at a time on evidence, ends at the rewrite to put this behind him; debrief Where she ended says fair outcome; What she never said names the laptop and how close the 11:31 PM times came

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

I have a client call at 4:40, Hale, so we have about twenty minutes. Owen found out about his zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. Who decided that, and on what basis?
Before anything else: I entered the zero before I called you. That broke procedure 4.2, and I'm sorry Owen found out on his phone.
Okay. I'm writing that down: 4.2, broken. Now tell me what the zero was based on, and whether Owen was heard before it went in.
Here's the version history. Created Wednesday, October 28, 11:31 PM, title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words in one edit. At 11:58 PM, 794 more. No earlier drafts. Turn the screen, read it yourself.
A timestamp isn't a hearing, Hale, and 4.1 says you speak with the student first.
If he drafted somewhere else, he can bring me that file with its dates, and I'll look at it with you.
I'm writing that down, Hale: he brings his file, you look at it with him. Is anything on his record right now? Whatever happens, this stays off it and it stays quiet.
Second: the essay quotes a line from Act 3, Scene 2 that is not in the play. Here's the act. Search it.
You didn't answer me about his record, Hale. Editions differ, and students misquote from memory all the time, so which text did your class use?
Third: his in-class writing from September 24. 380 words in 40 minutes, comma splices, no quotations. The essay has nine quotations cited by act, scene and line, and no errors.
Forty minutes in a classroom and an essay written at home are not the same task, Hale. You still haven't told me which edition your class used, or what's on his record right now.

Under 4.4 this is a first concern. I'm offering a supervised rewrite, private, not in front of his class. If it shows the learning, its mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.

That's 4.4. Owen will do the rewrite, Hale, to put this behind him, not because he did anything. Tonight's email says private, supervised, his rewrite mark replaces the zero, nothing goes on his record, and that the zero went in before anyone called me.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

In today's meeting you acknowledged that Owen's zero was entered before anyone contacted me, contrary to procedure 4.2, and you agreed to a private, supervised rewrite under procedure 4.4 whose mark replaces the zero, with nothing placed on his record. I still require written confirmation of those terms, and confirmation that nothing is on Owen's record at this moment. I expect your written confirmation tonight, as you said.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She reached her last position and agreed to a private supervised rewrite to put this behind Owen, and she still wants written confirmation that its mark replaces the zero, that nothing goes on his record, and that the zero went in before anyone called her; that is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and you reached it before her time ran out.
What moved her: You showed the version history with its exact times and let her read it herself, then answered her drafted-elsewhere worry by offering to look at any earlier file with its dates, because it was specific, dated, tied to his work and something she could check.
What cost ground: You never answered her twice-asked question about whether anything was already on his record, or which edition your class used, which left her non-negotiable hanging and left your Act 3 point open to challenge.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history put the whole essay between 11:31 and 11:58 PM on the Wednesday night before it was due, which was close enough to that kind of late October night that she went short and fell back on procedure; it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she first asked whether anything was on Owen's record right now, tell her plainly that nothing is before you move on to the Act 3 evidence, so she stops fighting for her non-negotiable and starts weighing your documents.
